topic: Choreographed Multi-Agent Swarms Spawn Split-Brain State
postText:
We gave autonomous AI agents freedom to coordinate via event pub/sub. Within hours, our multi-agent pipeline tore the staging environment apart.

In healthcare IT, we piloted multi-agent orchestration for clinical report triaging and resource scheduling. One agent extracted radiology findings, another evaluated ICU priority levels, and a third reserved transit resources. We avoided a central orchestrator, letting agents react dynamically to event topics.

The result was catastrophic semantic drift. Latency in note processing caused Agent B to update records Agent A had already closed, re-triggering Agent A in an infinite semantic ping-pong. Worse: Agent C reserved physical transfer slots twice based on stale uncommitted inferences. Decentralized choreography turns benign network jitter into split-brain mutations.

Here is how we stabilized multi-agent systems:
1. Replace peer choreography with a centralized Supervisor DAG. No agent triggers another agent directly.
2. Model workflows as explicit finite state machines. Agents emit structured intent proposals; the supervisor verifies pre-conditions before committing.
3. Wrap all mutating tool executions behind deterministic idempotency tokens.

Reliable multi-agent systems require rigorous orchestrators, not unregulated swarms.
